core_obligations: Reduce to the case of a local ring and a prime containing the ideal, using that regularity can be tested after localisation (proof lines 8183-8200).
Compare the Koszul complex of the ideal before and after the flat base change and use the flat base change statement for its first homology (proof lines 8201-8220).
Conclude that the vanishing of the Koszul homology in positive degrees descends along the flat map, which is the statement (proof lines 8220-8232).
proof_roadmap: Localise at a prime containing the ideal and reduce to the local case (proof lines 8183-8200).
Apply flat base change for the Koszul homology to compare the two complexes (proof lines 8201-8220).
Read off the descent of regularity from the comparison (proof lines 8220-8232).
difficulty_reason: The lemma is a descent statement for regularity of an ideal along a flat local homomorphism, and its proof is a 50-line argument that follows the classical route through the Koszul complex. It fixes a prime containing the ideal, reduces to the local situation, and compares the Koszul homology before and after base change using the flatness of the map and the flat base change statement for Koszul homology proved in the same chapter. The reduction to the prime-local situation and the identification of the two Koszul complexes are both written out, so the proof is self-contained apart from the standard inputs it names.
